Guidance & outlook: And new prices are now in effect, and we expect a recovery going forward in Q2, Q3.
ICM and PLE margin pressure, as Mohan has explained, it is a timing issue and a price pass - through, and we expect that to be recovering well in this and the next quarter.
The guidance we gave, I mean, despite all these things, the guidance that we gave in our press release dated 25th May 2026, still holds for the year.
Growth & demand: India had a very good quarter in terms of the automotive numbers with the sector growing at about 22% and both passenger vehicle and 2-wheeler segments had a solid double-digit growth.
But EBITDA grew only by 4.2% with the margins down from almost 15% to 13%.
And sir, the very strong revenue growth of 28% in GCM.
Margins & costs: Margins went down 2.8% to 6.7%, primarily due to delayed price increases and in particularly in the aftermarket business.
Revenue is up 48%, EBITDA up 100%, margins close to double digits.

Because if you look at the consol margin if you look at the consol gross margin, contribution margin for us, we have seen a very healthy expansion given this is despite the pressure we have seen on the RM and the stand-alone of the India business and also considering that the overall raw material environment has been very inflationary.
Capex & expansion: And we have certain VAT recoveries in China, Canada and Germany, which was a part of the acquisitions that we had done there.
I think if you offset those two months revenues, the growth is around 23% or so actually because the acquisition completed end of May last year.

And another one is from a Japanese OEM, again, USD 1.2 million a year, lifetime of USD 6 million, but they are all going for different, different plants of ours, for Matamoros, for China, et cetera, and for probably some of them also going to Morocco.
Balance sheet & cash: The total debt level was INR776 crores as on June 2026.
Risks & challenges: As you all know, the Middle East conflict, the oil and commodity prices, trade restrictions and shipping disruptions continue to be in play.
Stand- alone margins came under pressure, and Mohan will be walking through that as to what happened and how it's going to be a temporary phenomenon for us.
First things, I think we need to recognize that we have strong headwinds that has hit us not in terms of the market itself, market is doing good, but the raw material prices are really gone sky high.

Guidance & outlook: So, just to let the quarterly trajectory, which happened in FY26 was in Q1, we were at almost (-20%) EBITDA.
And we are expecting that this year to the EBITDA margin to be 10% to 12%.

I think that is the reason why margin slight drop is there 2% at the Phoenix Lamps Division, which is what we are expecting to recover this year, because this year, first of all, the growth is expected to come back for various reasons, including we talked about the world's largest retail chain is started buying to us.
Growth & demand: Again, on automotive growth of about 10-11%, our growth has been slightly lower.
Full-year revenue grew about 17% and EBITDA grew also by about 19-20%.
So, if you look at the overall picture, there is a slight growth, which is probably 1% or 2%, but there is no degrowth.
Margins & costs: So, SCD revenue grew by around (+10%) and EBITDA, for the first time margin, went to double digit.
The revenues declined by around 3% and EBITDA also declined.
Consolidated EBITDA, we are guiding for a 12 % to 13.5% range for the year.
Capex & expansion: Finally, just a quick note on the CAPEX for the year and to achieve the growth plan we are expecting: Suprajit Engineering Limited May 26, 2026 We have a CAPEX allocated for about INR 200 crores.
This is covering AURIC Maharashtra land purchase, STC building completion, SAL Chennai Plant -2, and the SCD capacity expansion.
So, if you look at employee cost to sales ratio, for example, right, I think, post LDC acquisition and SES acquisitions, it has been hovering between, like, say, 21% to 25%.
Balance sheet & cash: We have declared a higher dividend overall for the year, INR 3.50 per share against last year's INR 3.00.
